teams.heading: Fiji Rugby confirm interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for World Cup
teams.body: Fiji Rugby has confirmed its interest in recruiting Mark Nawaqanitawase for the 2027 World Cup in Australia. Fiji are in Pool C there with Argentina, Canada and Spain, and the interest comes as Jake White, named from 31 applicants on Tuesday, prepares for his first match in charge, against Japan. The team are ranked 10th in the world, so every addition to the squad matters.

lead.why: It is a player-specific squad story that is distinct from the Jake White appointment already run.

teams.heading: Henry Arundell could feature this weekend as Bath's England hopefuls edge closer
teams.body: Henry Arundell is closest to a comeback from Bath's injury list, with head of rugby Johann van Graan saying the England hopeful could even be in the mix this weekend. Arundell has missed the start of the campaign with a back issue. Fellow England hopefuls Will Muir, back in training after shoulder surgery, and Tom de Glanville, with a lower limb concern, have resumed parts of training, but there is no concrete return date for either, with availability assessed week by week.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item with named England hopefuls and a concrete availability update, and it does not repeat the Pearson story already run.

teams.heading: Dan Robson rates Maxime Lucu among world's best after 36-36 draw
teams.body: Gloucester's Dan Robson has called Bordeaux-Bègles fly-half Maxime Lucu one of the best in the world, and described his 803 kicking metres as ridiculous. Robson, who spent a season with Pau in the Top 14, said the overriding feeling in the Gloucester huddle after the 36-36 draw was disappointment. Lucu, a France star, ran Bordeaux's game from fly-half, while Gloucester's scrum finished at 100 per cent success against 67.

lead.why: It is a new France-linked item not already run, and it names a France player, Maxime Lucu, through his own club form rather than repeating the Ramos or Attissogbe stories.

teams.heading: Will Greenwood suggests Farrell try Ciaran Frawley at inside centre
teams.body: Will Greenwood, the 2003 England World Cup winner, suggests Andy Farrell pick Ciaran Frawley at inside centre alongside Sam Prendergast. Frawley, who left Leinster earlier this year for Connacht, has 15 Test caps, nearly all as a replacement. With Jack Crowley injured, he is now seen as a genuine rival to Sam Prendergast at 10. Farrell names his squad for the Argentina, Fiji and South Africa window today.

lead.why: It is a new Ireland selection debate with a named player and a fresh injury link, and it is not a repeat of the squad-announcement story already run today.

teams.heading: Italy, 11th of 12 after three straight defeats, face South Africa next
teams.body: Italy are 11 of 12 in the log, with three defeats from three matches, 37 points scored and 131 conceded. Their most recent outing was a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round three. The next assignment is South Africa in Round four, and the last meeting saw Italy lose 32-14 at home in November 2025 in the International Friendlies.

teams.heading: Tavi Tuipulotu dreams of running out for Scotland after Glasgow debut try
teams.body: Tavi Tuipulotu, brother of Scotland captain Sione and Edinburgh's Mosese, says he dreams of running out for Scotland himself. He marked his Glasgow debut with a try, and the episode, hosted by Andy Burke and Tom English, covers the chaos of growing up in the household. The episode also covers Glasgow's strong Champions Cup start. It is a useful bit of colour for a fan tracking the next Scotland squad.

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new Scotland item in the pack, and its subject is a Scotland ambition rather than club business alone.

teams.heading: Tandy hands uncapped trio Owen, Hope and Barratt Wales squad places
teams.body: Steve Tandy's 39-man squad for the November Tests includes three uncapped players: Dragons centre Aneurin Owen, scrum-half Che Hope and Cardiff loosehead Rhys Barratt. Owen gets his chance with Ben Thomas injured, and Tandy says Hope is "a really exciting talent" after strong Dragons form. Dewi Lake captains the group, and Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff before a southern hemisphere opponent at Twickenham.

lead.why: The highest-scoring new item, with two outlets covering three uncapped call-ups for the November Tests.

teams.heading: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil submit joint 2035 World Cup bid
teams.body: Argentina is leading a joint bid with Uruguay, Chile and Brazil to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, a push reported on 6 October. Union president Félix Páez Molina called it "a very important step for Argentine rugby and for the entire region". Eight Argentine grounds, from Buenos Aires' Monumental to Rosario's Gigante de Arroyito, feature in the proposal. World Rugby will announce its venues in November 2027.

teams.heading: Women's WXV: Aicha Sutcliffe makes first Scotland start against Wallaroos in Canberra
teams.body: Scotland women's interim head coach Dave Butcher has given Aicha Sutcliffe her first start, one of three changes for the final women's WXV Global Series match against the Wallaroos in Canberra. It is Sutcliffe's third consecutive match against Australia, and Scotland, beaten 56-12 in Sydney, are still seeking a first win of the competition. Sarah Bonar returns from illness in the second row, and Chloe Rollie is back at full-back.

lead.why: The only NEW item with a named Australia-side storyline; it is a women's story, so it is labelled as such.

teams.heading: Hajime Shoji's League One reverses plan to treat naturalised players as foreigners
teams.body: In late August, League One backtracked on registration rules that would have treated some naturalised players as foreigners despite their Japanese passports. The league granted an exception for players who had acquired or applied for citizenship by May 2025, after legal challenges and a fierce backlash. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted: "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes." The wider system was designed to cut places for foreign-born players eligible to represent Japan.

lead.why: It is the only candidate on Japan's men's eligibility pool, and no other item is new to today's edition.

teams.heading: All Blacks ran out early to honour Nathan Charles before Sydney Test
teams.body: The All Blacks brought their exit from the changing room forward of their own accord before the second Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, so they could greet Nathan Charles on the field. The former Wallabies hooker, who has revealed his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis, was acknowledged by players from both sides, and the whole team went over to him. Codie Taylor presented Charles with a framed jersey signed by the squad, and the All Blacks performed haka for him.

lead.why: A new, human-interest team story about the All Blacks' gesture to Nathan Charles, which is not a pundit opinion piece and does not repeat the McKenzie item already run.

teams.heading: Springboks face injury crisis three weeks before Paris clash with France
teams.body: The Springboks' build-up to the France Test in Paris has been hit by an injury crisis, with the match three weeks away. Today's coverage does not name the players affected or detail how many are out, so the scale of the problem remains unclear. South Africa's second Nations Championship leg runs through Italy, France and Ireland before the finals weekend in London, which leaves little room for absences.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item about the national men's side, though the pack carries only the headline, so the body stays deliberately thin.
